newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks stretch gains on FOMC hopes, Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks stretch gains on FOMC hopes, Dow.

text.p: The Mexican bourse extended early gains and was above the psychological 5,000-point barrier at midday trade on Tuesday.
Dealers said shares rose on moderate capital inflow amid market expectations the Federal Open Market Committee was not about to raise U.S. interest rates.

"We're beginning to see some foreign buying, as the Dow is up and fears of U.S. rate hikes have almost faded away," a floor trader said. The leading IPC share index was up 62.30 points, or 1.26 percent, at 5,015.18.
The Dow Jones had meanwhile risen 62.25 points to 7,865.61.
The Fed panel was expected to make an announcement at 1315 local time, or some two hours before the close of stock trading.
Dealers said strong GDP data released on Monday were having a delayed effect on stocks.
"Obviously GDP data are helping today. They made no impact yesterday because the market was nervous," a dealer said.
Traders said market caution remained and could be seen in thin volume of 40.3 million shares.
Market heavyweights Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and Bancomer were the most traded gainers.
Telmex was up 15 centavos to 20.35 percent, while the telecom's ADRs had advanced 7/8 to 52-7/16. Financial firm Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest, had meanwhile gained six centavos to 5.30 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers outnumbered sliders by 58 to 26.
